name: The Moirai Severance

detectability.signature: Sensor feeds returning answers before queries are submitted; paradox warnings cascading across whole sectors

proximity: Effect precedes cause in sensor data; damage reports log before any impact occurs
Crew actions complete before the decision to make them
contact: Events unravel mid-occurrence; wounds heal as blows land somewhere else
Vessel systems act on orders given in futures that then cancel
prolonged_exposure: Personal timelines sever; crew members cease ever to have existed
Reality breakdown spreading along the wake the anomaly leaves behind

description: The Severance resembles a tear through a painted sky: ragged volumes where starlight arrives out of order and colors contradict their own spectra. Across nearly a third of an astronomical unit, effects precede their causes like thunder preceding lightning, and instruments report battles that have not yet begun. Charts mark the region with the oldest symbol cartography permits: a plain black X.

The fracture grows, patiently and without rhythm, its tendrils probing neighboring space like roots seeking water. Within it, events start, abort, and complete in contradictory sequences; a ship may take damage from an attack that then never happens. Outside, records warp: logs rewrite overnight, and bereaved families receive condolences for deaths their own memories insist never occurred.

The destroyer Vigilant Knot engaged the anomaly and won a battle her surviving crew cannot remember fighting; the victory is documented, decorated, and universally dreaded. Downstream systems mourn colonies whose founding records have ceased to exist. Every attempt to study the Severance has produced results that arrive before the experiments are proposed.

Quarantine buoys now ring the fracture at extreme range, listening for the paradox warnings that precede each expansion. Cults and physicists share the outer stations, the former praying and the latter taking notes on the prayers' efficacy. The thread has not yet been cut; the open question is whether anything still holds the scissors.
